title: A Business That Shares Its Tools
title_ja: 道具を共有するビジネス
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空事例。実在の企業や実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: Some products are useful precisely because they are available at the moment when someone needs them, even if they remain unused for much of the rest of the year.
sentences.ja: 製品の中には、残りの一年の大半に使われなくても、必要な瞬間に利用できるからこそ有用なものがある。

sentences.en: A tool used for an occasional repair may occupy storage space for months without contributing directly to any activity.
sentences.ja: 時折の修理に使う道具は何か月も活動に直接貢献せず保管場所を占めることがある。

sentences.en: Purchasing such a tool can nevertheless be a reasonable decision if obtaining it elsewhere would be inconvenient or expensive.
sentences.ja: 別の場所で得ることが不便または高価なら、その道具の購入も合理的判断になり得る。

sentences.en: The value of ownership consequently depends partly on the alternatives available to the person who needs the product.
sentences.ja: したがって所有の価値は、製品を必要とする人に利用可能な代替手段にも依存する。

sentences.en: Imagine a business that rents household tools to residents of a small town.
sentences.ja: 小さな町の住民に家庭用の道具を貸す事業を想像しよう。

sentences.en: Its owner initially estimates that many customers will prefer renting to purchasing because they use the equipment only occasionally.
sentences.ja: 経営者は当初、機器を時折しか使わないため多くの顧客が購入よりレンタルを好むと見積もる。

sentences.en: However, several customers explain that they hesitate to rent tools because they cannot predict exactly when a problem will arise.
sentences.ja: しかし複数の顧客は問題がいつ起きるか正確に予測できないので道具を借りるのをためらうと説明する。

sentences.en: For them, immediate access may matter more than the difference between the total cost of buying and renting.
sentences.ja: 彼らには購入とレンタルの総費用の差より即時利用が重要かもしれない。

sentences.en: The owner decides to examine how customers actually expect to use the service.
sentences.ja: 経営者は顧客が実際にどうサービスを使うつもりか調べることを決める。

sentences.en: Some can reserve equipment in advance because their projects follow a planned schedule.
sentences.ja: 予定された日程に従い作業するので事前に予約できる人もいる。

sentences.en: Others need to know whether a suitable tool will be available at short notice.
sentences.ja: 急な連絡でも適切な道具を使えるか知る必要のある人もいる。

sentences.en: Providing both types of access might require the business to maintain some equipment that is not continuously rented.
sentences.ja: 両方の利用を提供するには継続的には貸し出されない機器も維持する必要があるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The business considers publishing information about availability and offering a reservation system with clearly stated conditions.
sentences.ja: 事業は利用可能状況の公開と条件を明示した予約制度の提供を検討する。

sentences.en: It also needs to account for inspection, maintenance and the time required to prepare returned equipment for another customer.
sentences.ja: 点検、維持、返却機器を次の顧客に準備する時間も考慮する必要がある。

sentences.en: The fictional example does not establish that renting is generally cheaper or environmentally preferable to buying.
sentences.ja: 架空例はレンタルが購入より一般的に安いことや環境上望ましいことを確立しない。

sentences.en: Instead, it shows why a service must be assessed in relation to the circumstances of its intended users.
sentences.ja: 代わりにサービスを想定利用者の事情に照らして評価すべき理由を示す。

sentences.en: Ownership and access are two different ways of meeting a practical need.
sentences.ja: 所有と利用機会は実際の必要を満たす二つの異なる方法だ。

sentences.en: A lower price is meaningful only when the alternative service can provide the kind of access that the customer requires.
sentences.ja: 代替サービスが顧客の必要とする利用機会を提供できるときに限り、低価格は意味を持つ。

sentences.en: Businesses that recognize this distinction can ask more precise questions about what their customers value.
sentences.ja: この区別を認識する事業は顧客が何に価値を置くかより正確な問いを問える。

sentences.en: The shared tool is therefore not merely a physical product but part of a service organized around availability.
sentences.ja: したがって共有道具は単なる物理的製品でなく利用可能性を中心に組織されたサービスの一部だ。

vocabulary.definition: act of keeping for future use
ability to reach or use something

questions.prompt: Why might someone purchase a rarely used tool?
options: They may value immediate access when it is needed.
It necessarily creates income every day.
Every rental service charges the same price.
questions.explanation_ja: 必要な時に使える価値。

questions.prompt: What does the value of ownership partly depend on?
options: The size of the town alone.

questions.prompt: What service does the imaginary business offer?
Why do some customers hesitate to rent?
options: The owner has refused all rentals.
questions.explanation_ja: 必要時期が予測できない。

questions.prompt: Which customers can reserve in advance?
questions.explanation_ja: 計画された作業のある人。

questions.prompt: Why might idle equipment be useful to the business?
options: It can help meet unexpected demand.
It proves that no customer rents anything.
It guarantees every tool is safe.

questions.prompt: What costs or tasks must the business consider?
Why does the author qualify the fictional example?
options: It proves renting is superior in every case.
It does not establish universal economic or environmental benefits.
It establishes a legal rental requirement.
questions.explanation_ja: 一般的な優位性は実証していない。

options: The ability to obtain and use something.
The act of selling a business.

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: A rental service's value depends on whether it meets users' actual needs for availability.
Renting is always cheaper than ownership.
A business should rent every tool continuously.
The cheapest option always serves every customer.
questions.explanation_ja: 利用条件に合うかが重要。

paraphrases.source: Some products are useful precisely because they are available at the moment when someone needs them, even if they remain unused for much of the rest of the year.
paraphrases.rewrite: A product may be valuable despite being unused for long periods.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 使わない期間が長くても価値がある。

paraphrases.source: However, several customers explain that they hesitate to rent tools because they cannot predict exactly when a problem will arise.
paraphrases.rewrite: Customers hesitate because they do not know when a need will occur.

paraphrases.source: Providing both types of access might require the business to maintain some equipment that is not continuously rented.
paraphrases.rewrite: Serving planned and unexpected demand may require keeping some tools available.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 二種類の需要に備える。

paraphrases.source: The shared tool is therefore not merely a physical product but part of a service organized around availability.
paraphrases.rewrite: The shared tool belongs to a service focused on access, not just a collection of objects.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 物だけでなく利用機会。

discourse.role_ja: 低頻度使用でも購入の合理性。
予想された需要と利用者の懸念。
一般的優位の主張でなく例の意義。
